tokens.name: canvas
tokens.usage: Page background behind the reading sheet. Compose: colorScheme.background.

tokens.name: sheet
tokens.usage: The reading sheet that holds a lesson's text. Compose: colorScheme.surface.

tokens.name: sheet-sunken
tokens.usage: Blocks inside the sheet: callouts, checkpoints, diagram paper. Compose: surfaceVariant / surfaceContainer.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Body text and headings on sheet and sheet-sunken. Compose: onSurface.

tokens.name: ink-muted
tokens.usage: Captions, meta lines, eyebrows. Never for running text. Compose: onSurfaceVariant.

tokens.name: line
tokens.usage: Hairlines, table rules, the sheet's 1px edge. Compose: outlineVariant.

tokens.name: line-strong
tokens.usage: Diagram node outlines, control borders and edges at rest. At least 3:1 on canvas, sheet and sheet-sunken in every theme (light 3.64, dark 3.64, sepia 3.45 at worst). Compose: outline.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: Links, active tab, primary buttons, state flowing forward in diagrams. Compose: primary.

tokens.name: on-accent
tokens.usage: Text and icons on an accent fill. Compose: onPrimary.

tokens.name: accent-soft
tokens.usage: Tint for Start here and staff-note callouts, inline code background. Compose: primaryContainer.

tokens.name: event
tokens.usage: The second direction in a diagram: events, requests, replies travelling back. Compose: secondary.

tokens.name: event-soft
tokens.usage: Tint behind event-coloured labels and the Remember callout. Compose: secondaryContainer.

tokens.name: warn
tokens.usage: Blocked, failing or under-review states: queued packets, Under review notes. Compose: error.

tokens.name: warn-soft
tokens.usage: Tint behind Under review notes. Compose: errorContainer.

tokens.name: grid-dot
tokens.usage: The dot grid on diagram paper, one dot per space-4.

tokens.name: focus
tokens.usage: 2px keyboard focus ring on every interactive element.

tokens.name: code-bg
tokens.usage: Code card background. Code stays dark in every theme.

tokens.name: code-key
tokens.usage: Kotlin keywords and annotations on code-bg.

tokens.name: code-call
tokens.usage: Function and type names on code-bg.

tokens.name: code-string
tokens.usage: String and number literals on code-bg.

tokens.name: code-comment
tokens.usage: Comments on code-bg (still 4.5:1; comments carry meaning in this playbook).

tokens.name: scene-client
tokens.usage: Illustrated screens and callers; shape and labels identify the role too.

tokens.name: scene-runtime
tokens.usage: Illustrated compute, workers and platform services.

tokens.name: scene-storage
tokens.usage: Illustrated data, retained state and memory.

tokens.name: scene-queue
tokens.usage: Illustrated queues and parcels. Warning state still uses warn.

tokens.name: glow-1
tokens.usage: Soft canvas glow behind the sheet (dark theme).

tokens.name: preview-light-bg
tokens.usage: Theme picker swatch: light background, shown whatever theme is active.

tokens.name: preview-dark-bg
tokens.usage: Theme picker swatch: dark background, shown whatever theme is active.

tokens.name: preview-sepia-bg
tokens.usage: Theme picker swatch: sepia background, shown whatever theme is active.

tokens.name: preview-contrast-bg
tokens.usage: Theme picker swatch: contrast background, shown whatever theme is active.

fonts.usage: Interface, navigation, headings, tables and captions.
Modern Sans prose (subset of Source Sans 3; renamed because 'Source' is a Reserved Font Name).
Book Serif prose (subset of Source Serif 4, optical size 18; renamed for the same reason).
Handwritten prose. No italic file: the browser slants it, which suits a handwriting face and saves 89KB.

families.mono: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
families.modern: "Playbook Sans", "Playbook Sans Fallback", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
families.classic: "Times New Roman", Times, "Liberation Serif", "Noto Serif", serif
families.easy: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next", "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Fallback", system-ui, sans-serif

styles.name: displayLarge
styles.usage: Lesson title (H1), once per page. Inter 700; headings never follow the reading font.

styles.name: headlineMedium
styles.sample: Phase 8: Build tooling and OS internals

styles.name: bodyLarge
styles.sample: A method call that looks local can wait on another process's busy thread.
styles.usage: Running lesson prose in the reader's chosen font (--font-prose, default Modern Sans). The reader's size setting scales it; paragraphs are spaced 1.1em and capped at the prose measure.

styles.name: bodyMedium
styles.sample: Illustrative timing. Every step is also readable as text.
styles.usage: Captions, table cells, checkpoint labels and UI text (Inter).

styles.name: labelSmall
styles.usage: Eyebrows and callout labels, set in capitals.

styles.name: codeBlock
styles.usage: Code cards, 0.86em of the surrounding text. Ligatures off so -> and != look as typed.

styles.name: codeInline
styles.usage: Inline code in running text (0.85em of the surrounding text).

styles.name: handNode
styles.usage: Labels inside diagram nodes and stepper boxes.

styles.name: handNote
styles.sample: state flows right, events flow back
styles.usage: One annotation per diagram, and edge labels. Never for text the reader must parse to answer a question.

fallbacks.usage: Local system faces scaled to each web font's average advance and vertical metrics (website/tools/build_fonts.py --fallbacks), so text barely moves when the web font swaps in. Measured against Arial and Times New Roman.

prose.usage: The reader's font choice. It sets --font-prose, which only paragraphs, list items, blockquotes, reading callouts and Q&A prose use. Headings, interface, tables, code and diagrams never follow it.

options.label: Modern Sans
options.description: A calm, open sans for long reading. The default.

options.label: Book Serif
options.description: A text serif with the feel of a printed book.

options.label: Classic Serif
options.description: Times New Roman from your device. Some devices substitute a similar serif.

options.label: Handwritten
options.description: An informal, marker-style hand designed for reading on screen.

options.label: Easy Read
options.description: Developed to increase legibility for readers with low vision, with distinctive letterforms that are hard to confuse. Some readers find it easier; others prefer Modern Sans.

metrics.measureUsage: Each option's measure is the prose width, in em of the prose text, that gives a median of about 70 characters per line; calibrated by rendering lesson paragraphs. Code, tables and diagrams keep the full text column (measure-text).

code.usage: Every code surface: code cards, playground editor, diagram code pairs and correction excerpts (0.86em, line height 1.6). Inline code in prose uses 0.85em.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Gap between an icon and its label.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Gap inside chips and between stacked labels.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Gap between diagram nodes on phones.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Minimum page gutter; diagram grid pitch; callout padding on phones.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Callout and code-card padding; gap between paragraphs and blocks.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Sheet padding on tablets; gap before an H3.

tokens.name: space-12
tokens.usage: Sheet padding on desktop; gap before an H2.

tokens.name: radius-md
tokens.usage: Diagram nodes, callouts, checkpoints, code cards.

tokens.name: radius-lg
tokens.usage: The reading sheet and the lesson hero.

tokens.name: shadow-sheet
tokens.usage: The reading sheet only. Nothing inside the sheet has a shadow.

tokens.name: shadow-visual-frame
tokens.usage: Soft depth for wide visuals, with no shadow in highcontrast.

tokens.name: measure-text
tokens.usage: Maximum width of the text column: code cards, tables and diagrams use all of it. Prose is capped at the reading font's own measure (type.prose), about 70 characters a line.

tokens.name: measure-wide
tokens.usage: Maximum width of the sheet including its padding (box-sizing: border-box). Code cards never exceed measure-text; only diagrams, step-throughs and overflowing tables may break out wider.

tokens.name: rail-left
tokens.usage: Curriculum sidebar width. Shown only from 1440px (244 + 880 sheet + 220 outline + 2 x 48 gutters); below that it collapses into the menu.

tokens.name: rail-right
tokens.usage: In-this-chapter outline width. Shown from 1181px (880 sheet + 220 + gutters); below that the outline moves to the top of the sheet.

tokens.name: measure-visual
tokens.usage: Maximum width for wide diagrams and other overflowing visual content. Normal sheet and prose measures remain unchanged; breakout is symmetric and viewport/rail limited.

tokens.name: reading-prose-measure
tokens.usage: Approved prose fills the established760px reading column for every readerfont.

tokens.name: visual-bleed
tokens.usage: Maximum symmetric extension per side of a wide visual.

tokens.name: visual-frame-padding
tokens.usage: Shared roomy frame padding on desktop/tablet.

tokens.name: visual-frame-gap
tokens.usage: Space connecting a framed visual to surrounding prose.

tokens.name: walkthrough-sticky-top
tokens.usage: InterviewWalkthrough: where the pacing bar sticks on wide screens, just below the sticky top bar and lesson tabs.

tokens.name: walkthrough-progress-height
tokens.usage: InterviewWalkthrough: height reserved for the sticky pacing bar, added to the anchor scroll offset.

tokens.name: walkthrough-step-min
tokens.usage: InterviewWalkthrough: narrowest timeline step card before the list wraps to fewer columns.

tokens.name: walkthrough-card-min
tokens.usage: InterviewWalkthrough: narrowest decision card before the trade-off grid wraps to fewer columns.

tokens.name: scene-step-select-min
tokens.usage: FlowScene: minimum width for the compact named-step selector before it wraps.

tokens.name: scene-loss-stroke
